verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The paper's single tuple bound is two conjuncts in Lean: Result.tail_velocity for the velocity entry and Result.tail_scalars for the pressure/stress entries, with different explicit losses (max(cutLoss L (m+1), cutLoss L m) + 1 against cutLoss L m — the extra derivative being the curl). Taking ℓ'_m to be the larger of the two gives the paper's statement; both are functions of m and L only, so the paper's 'ℓ'_m is independent of J' holds. Constants and the domain condition match exactly: (1/2)^J = 2^{-J}, exponent g(J+1)/2 - ℓ'_m, condition q w < 1/(2 a_J). Two conventions: (i) Lean bounds ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m‖ at exactly order m while the paper's |V|_m of (5.23) is the pointwise max of ∂_x^α ∂_t^b V over |α|+b ≤ m; since a j ≥ 1 forces q < 1/2 and cutLoss is nondecreasing in m, the order-k bound for k ≤ m is itself ≤ 2^{-J} q^{g(J+1)/2 - ℓ'_m}, and each partial derivative is a value of iteratedFDeriv on unit coordinate vectors, so the Lean bounds imply the paper's max. (ii) Lean's order range is m ≤ J+2 (velocity) and m ≤ J+3 (scalars) with no lower bound on J, which contains the paper's range J ≥ max(1,m).
